spec_match.rationale: Composes a user controller with a second signal via AbortSignal.any(), aborts either half, and classifies solely from what response.text() threw — the TimeoutError-vs-custom-reason distinction the feature exists to enable.

interactive.rationale: Start/Cancel/Let-it-time-out buttons drive real fetches; verified the cancel path produced the outcome panel, the evidence table and log entries.

blurb_alignment.rationale: The card promises distinguishing retry-worthy timeouts from silent user cancels, which is the page's classifier.

edge_cases.rationale: Body-finished-before-abort, fetch-promise rejection, and the pre-154 indistinguishable state each get a distinct honest verdict, and the button-driven timeout is openly documented as a demo convenience.

conformance.rationale: The suite covers AbortSignal.any composition and TimeoutError vocabulary alongside the forwarding assertions; on Chromium 141 /conformance/ reported 5 pass / 2 fail with the two forwarding assertions honestly failing.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Chromium 141 headless (cloud, no chrome-devtools-mcp): started a request, cancelled mid-body — outcome read 'Indistinguishable: AbortError' with the rose styling, the evidence table showed the user signal.reason present but undelivered (error.code 20, not USER_CANCEL), and the detail correctly attributed this to pre-154 behaviour; console clean, intentional ERR_ABORTED only.

telemetry_health.rationale: Loads demo-telemetry.js and emits an abort-classified assert with kind and error name.

design_system.rationale: CSS variables, outcome states use amber/emerald/rose accents with text titles, secondary buttons override both colours, no static card.

accessibility.rationale: aria-live log and detail, evidence table with scoped row headers, outcome conveyed by title text alongside colour, labelled 44px buttons.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: No horizontal overflow at 360x740 DPR3 (scrollWidth 360, screenshot read); button row wraps.

openQuestions.title: Consider a real AbortSignal.timeout() variant alongside the button-driven one
openQuestions.detail: The 'Let it time out now' button aborts a second controller with a hand-made TimeoutError DOMException so visitors need not wait, which the note explains. A small optional mode ('use a real 3s AbortSignal.timeout()') would let the page also demonstrate the platform-generated TimeoutError end to end — including that its reason is set by the platform, matching the suite's timeout-signals-use-timeouterror assertion — at the cost of a three-second wait.

summary: Reviewed at http://localhost:3000/v154/fetch-api-forward-reason-from-abortcontroller-to-fetch-response/timeout-vs-user/ with Chromium 141 headless (cloud, no chrome-devtools-mcp). The classifier demo works and is honest on this pre-154 build: cancelling mid-body produced a substituted AbortError, the page classified it 'Indistinguishable', showed the undelivered signal.reason in its evidence table, and explained that Chrome 154 is what makes flag-free classification possible. Console clean (ERR_ABORTED entries are the demo's own aborts); desktop 1280 and mobile 360 DPR3 screenshots read, no overflow; /conformance/ reported 5 pass / 2 fail — the two Chrome-154 forwarding assertions. One minor idea: an optional real AbortSignal.timeout() path.
